## Says

- "That's a granny knot. Who taught you that? Not me."

    - So the water's been over my notch. Twice, the girl says. I cut that mark when I was ten. I don't like it, *Player*, and I'm too old to pretend I do.
    - The racks have been quiet since the gulls learned their lesson. That's one kind of tear I won't see for a while.
    - Still have your claws on my bench. I look at them now and then. They're honest, crabs.
    - Well? I can talk and mend at once. I've had fifty years' practice.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* What tears the nets?

    - Agna. I've mended the coves' nets fifty years, and my mother before me. Every boat on this shingle fishes with my knots, and they know it.
    - Sorcha's my girl. Loud as me, stubborn as me, which is why we argue. Calder's a good one, he mends without being asked. The magpie and Eilidh you'll have met. Everyone has.
    - Long bites through a dozen meshes at once. Not the ragged hole a seal leaves, not a clean cut off a rock. Always from boats that went out past the point.
    - I mend every one. And I say nothing in front of Eilidh, who notices everything. Ask me something else.
    - The crab work and the gull work I can mend half asleep. The long tears from past the point I mend wide awake. Ask me something else.
    - When I was young the boats went out on still summer nights with a lantern in every bow. From the shore you could count them, strung across the water like a second line of stars.
    - I went out with Maili more than once, her that married Varro the warden after. Nobody's fished at night here for twenty years. The young ones think I made it up. You don't. I can see.
    - Off with you. And retie that knot.
